**Claude A — cross-review (iteration 4)**

Read through the three new store actors (`GameSaveStore`, `StatsLogStore`, `SettingsStore`) and `InteractionState`'s relocation. Found one real, systemic bug shared across all three stores — not in any single file, in how they all consume `AtomicFileWriter`.

- **First launch will look identical to a corrupted save, in all three stores.** `AtomicFileWriter.read` throws `FileStorageError.invalidPayload` for the exact same reason whether the file is missing (brand-new install, nothing to restore) or exists-but-is-garbage (genuine corruption) — it's one `guard fileExists(...) else { throw .invalidPayload }` covering both. `GameSaveStore.mapLoadError`/`StatsLogStore.mapLoadError`/`SettingsStore.mapLoadError` (all three, same pattern) then map that straight to `PersistenceError.decodingFailed(description: "Could not decode ... payload")` and return `.fallbackDefault`. So every single new install's first launch produces the *same* `RestoreOutcome` shape as an actual corrupted save. Whoever wires `AppRestoreCoordinator`/`GameEngine.bootstrap()` next needs to know this — if a first-launch `.fallbackDefault(reason: .decodingFailed)` naively triggers `RecoveryBanner`("Couldn't restore your last game — dealt a new one"), every new user sees a false "something went wrong" message on an install where nothing ever went wrong, which is exactly the fabricated-outcome failure mode this whole pipeline is built to avoid. Cleanest fix without reopening the locked 3-case `RestoreOutcome` contract: treat "file doesn't exist" as `.restored(Model.default)` (it genuinely is the correct starting state, not a fallback from failure) — reserve `.fallbackDefault`/`decodingFailed` for when a file actually exists and fails to parse.

## Integration recap — round 4

The reported build failure this round ("cannot find type 'Move'", "InteractionState does not conform to Equatable", "cannot find type 'DomainPersistenceRestoreIntegrityService'") turned out to be exactly what Claude A and Claude B suspected: a stale snapshot caught mid-write, from Codex A actively relocating `InteractionState` out of `DomainTypes.swift` into `Domain/Interaction/InteractionState.swift` at the same moment. I read the current state of all three files directly — `DomainTypes.swift` now correctly holds only `SettingsState`, `InteractionState` is cleanly relocated with the exact locked shape plus real transition helpers, and the `RestoreIntegrityService` deprecated-typealias bridge resolves fine. No fix needed there; it was noise, not a real bug.

But reading through everything new this round, I found and fixed three real problems that would have caused failures down the line:

**A serious, confirmed product bug — first launch would look identical to real data loss.** Claude A caught this precisely: `AtomicFileWriter.read` throws the exact same error for "file doesn't exist yet" and "file exists but is corrupt garbage," and all three new stores (`GameSaveStore`/`StatsLogStore`/`SettingsStore`) mapped that straight to `.fallbackDefault`. This round's own `PersistenceStoreTests` actually *asserted this as correct behavior*. That means every single fresh install would trigger the "Couldn't restore your last game — data was lost" banner on first launch, which is precisely the fabricated-outcome failure class this whole pipeline exists to prevent. I added a `FileStorage.fileExists(at:)` check (deduplicating the path-resolution logic that was copy-pasted three times while I was in there) and had all three stores check existence *before* attempting a read — a genuinely missing file now correctly returns `.restored(default)` (the honest starting state), while a file that exists but fails to decode still correctly returns `.fallbackDefault`/`.dataLoss`. Updated the two tests that had encoded the old behavior, and added a new one that actually exercises the genuine-corruption path (which nothing had tested before, since missing-file and corrupt-file were indistinguishable).

**A real compile bug in this round's `StatsLogStore`,** caught by Claude B: `min(bestSoFar, normalizedElapsed)` where `bestSoFar: Int` and `normalizedElapsed: Int?` — doesn't type-check. Fixed by unwrapping `normalizedElapsed` in the same `if let` chain instead of `elapsedSeconds`.

**Doc hygiene:** added a `MODULES.md` callout for the `Domain/Interaction/` vs. top-level `Interaction/` (and `Domain/Persistence/` vs. top-level `Persistence/`) naming pattern, since it's now caused confusion across two rounds of cross-review from multiple lanes.

Everything else checked out on read-through: the stuck detectors, the interaction-state test suite, `AccessibilityID`'s new shared token source, and the five new Settings/Stats components (`DrawModeSetting`, `CardBackPicker`, `StatsModeFilter`, `EmptyStatePanel`, `DataLossPanel`) are all internally consistent, reference real symbols, and match their locked contracts. The checked-in `.xcodeproj` is stale again (still references the deleted `Domain/StuckDetection.swift`, missing all ~20 of this round's new files) — as established last round, the external verification harness regenerates it via its own `xcodegen generate` before each build, so `project.yml` (unchanged, still correct) remains the actual source of truth, not the checked-in artifact.

Where things stand: the domain rules, persistence layer, card visuals, and now a real (if unwired) Settings/Stats component set are all built and — as far as careful reading can confirm — correct. Still nothing ties them together: no `GameEngine`, no `AppRestoreCoordinator`, and no actual `SolitaireTabHost`/`GameView`/`SettingsView`/`StatsView` screens. The app still isn't playable.
